svg.title: Work admission: from entry point to provider turn
svg.desc: Web chat, channel messages, scheduled prompts and logical agents reach TurnManager; tasks and workflow steps reach TaskExecutor. Both ask ExecutionCoordinator for a lease: admission checks, then a primary-lane or worker-lane capacity permit, then a runner. TurnRunner runs the turn on the leased runner; a refusal at admission or capacity stops before any provider.

g.text: Hover a box for what it decides; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Work admission: from entry point to provider turn
Six entry points, one allocator. A turn that fails admission or finds no capacity never reaches a provider.

g.text: Web chat · ConversationService.submit admits the message (revision-checked; a busy session queues it and returns 202)
The browser then streams the turn from GET /api/sessions/<id>/stream?turn=<turnId>; TurnManager reserves the turn.
Channel message · handleInboundMessage resolves channel, session key and thread binding; ChannelTaskBridge may consume the message first
Unconsumed messages go to MessageQueue (per-session FIFO, 1000 ms debounce); bound to a logical agent, the turn takes the worker lane.
Scheduled prompt · a prompt job starts a turn through TurnManager.startTurn with TurnProvenance.cron()
A cron session takes the worker lane, or the primary lane only in the single-harness SDK composition.
Logical agent · MCP tools create or continue a configured logical-agent session
Admission is fail-fast: no capacity raises BusyTurnException instead of waiting.
Task · TaskExecutor polls queued tasks FIFO and asks for a worker lease for the task's provider and security profile
Fail-fast: a lane with no free permit leaves the task queued for the next poll.
Workflow step · an agent step runs as a workflow-owned task whose whole prompt chain uses one leased worker
Bash and approval steps are host-owned inside the engine and never reach the allocator.
TurnManager · entry for conversation turns: resolves provider, policy, workspace and provenance, then asks the coordinator for a lease
reserveTurn orders same-session reservations; on the lease, the leased runner gets reserveAdmittedTurn.
TaskExecutor · polls queued tasks, checks project and budget, and requests a worker lease itself
A polled fail-fast request takes its permit before admission, so an attempt the lane cannot run leaves no loop or rate-limit record.
Admission · TurnRunner.admitTurn: token budget (read-only check), session lock, then loop-chain check and global rate window
The lock precedes the two checks that record state. A lock wait warns at 30 s and reads as stuck at 120 s; the rate window waits, never refuses.
Lane and permit · the one capacity decision: the primary lane (fixed, serialized) or the worker lane (providers.<id>.pool_size)
Web chat takes the primary lane only when its provider and policy match the primary harness; container count never changes pool_size.
Lease · reuse an idle cached worker for the same provider, policy and session shape, else scavenge the oldest and build one
A container worker is reused only by a logical agent or a temporary conversation on the same session; otherwise it gets a fresh authority.
Refused · budget limit reached with action block, loop detected with action abort, or a busy session or lane
The caller gets the refusal; admission and permit are released, so nothing was recorded for a turn that never ran.
TurnRunner · runs the turn on the leased runner: reserveAdmittedTurn, then executeTurn
Guard evaluation on hook callbacks, message persistence, BridgeEvent streaming, stall and wall-clock limits, cost tracking.
Provider binary · the harness owned by the leased runner spawns and drives the provider binary
Container or host for claude and codex; ACP agents run on the host only.
